title: Maximum profit in job scheduling
pattern: weighted intervals: sort by end, DP + binary search
statement: Job i runs on [start[i], end[i]) with a profit. Choose non-overlapping jobs (a job may start exactly when another ends) to maximise total profit. n ≤ 3 × 10⁴, times ≤ 10⁹.

solution.explanation: Weights break Part 5's earliest-end greedy, which is the trap: it's DP. Sort by end; dp[i] = best using the first i jobs = max(skip job i, take it + dp[last job ending ≤ its start]). The predecessor is a binary search over the sorted ends. Times up to 10⁹ rule out a DP over time.
solution.python:
import bisect

import bisect

def job_scheduling(start, end, profit):
    jobs = sorted(zip(end, start, profit))
    ends = [e for e, _, _ in jobs]
    dp = [0] * (len(jobs) + 1)
    for i, (e, s, p) in enumerate(jobs):
        j = bisect.bisect_right(ends, s, 0, i)
        dp[i + 1] = max(dp[i], dp[j] + p)
    return dp[-1]
